stages.title: Intermediate vocabulary
stages.hook: What is the difference between "often" and "sometimes"? Small frequency and reason words make your Chinese sound richer.
explain: Intermediate vocabulary adds words that connect ideas and show how often or how sure you are. 经常 (jīngcháng) means often, 有时候 (yǒushíhou) means sometimes, 已经 (yǐjīng) means already, and 一定 (yídìng) means certainly. These adverbs go before the verb.
觉得 (juéde) means to feel or to think, and is used for opinions: 我觉得汉语很有意思 (I think Chinese is interesting). 因为 (yīnwèi) gives a reason and 所以 (suǒyǐ) gives a result. 但是 (dànshì) means but.
Many Chinese words are made of two characters whose meanings combine. 图书馆 (túshūguǎn) is picture-book-hall, a library. Learning the single characters helps you guess new words.
stages.mnemonic: Often 经常, sometimes 有时候: adverbs stand before the verb.
sentences: He often goes to the library.
Because it is raining, I stay at home.

gq.q: Where does 经常 go in a sentence?
gq.why: Frequency adverbs go before the verb.

panel.q: What is the best way to say "I think it is good"?
panel.why: 觉得 introduces an opinion.

panel.q: Why can knowing single characters help with new words?
panel.why: Many compound words combine the meanings of their characters, such as 图书馆.

panel.q: Which pair shows reason then result?
panel.why: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 gives the result.

teach.model: Words like 经常 often and 已经 already go before the verb. 觉得 is for opinions. 因为 gives a reason and 所以 gives the result.

points.ask: Where do these adverbs go?
How do I give an opinion?
How do I link a reason and a result?

trip.prompt: Find how two characters can make a new word and give one example.

stages.title: Verb forms and time expressions
stages.hook: "I ate", "I have been to China", "I am eating". Mandarin has no past tense ending. So how does it show time?
explain: Mandarin shows time with time words and aspect particles, not verb endings. 了 (le) after the verb marks a completed action: 我吃了 (I have eaten). 过 (guo) marks experience: 我去过中国 (I have been to China). 着 (zhe) marks a continuing state: 门开着 (the door is open).
For an action in progress, use 正在 or 在 before the verb: 他正在看书 means he is reading. For something about to happen, use 就要…了: 火车就要开了 means the train is about to leave.
The future is often shown by 会 (huì) or by a time word such as 明天: 明天我会去. Negatives differ: 没 (méi) denies completed actions (我没吃), while 不 (bù) denies habits or intentions (我不吃).
stages.mnemonic: 了 done, 过 been there, 着 still going, 在 right now.
sentences: The train is about to leave.

gq.q: Which sentence says "I have been to China" as an experience?
How do you say "I did not eat"?

panel.q: What is the difference between 我不吃 and 我没吃?
o: 不 is past and 没 is future
不 for habit or will, 没 for something that did not happen
panel.why: 不 negates a habit or will; 没 negates a past or completed event.

panel.q: Why is there no verb ending for the past in Mandarin?
o: Time is shown by words and particles
panel.why: Chinese uses time words and aspect particles instead of tense endings.

panel.q: What does 门开着 describe?
o: The door is open (and stays open)
The door is opening and closing
panel.why: 着 shows a state that continues.

teach.model: Mandarin does not change verb endings for tense. Instead 了 shows a completed action, 过 shows experience, 着 a continuing state and 在 an action in progress. 没 negates past events.

points.ask: How do I show something is done?
And something I have experienced?
How do I negate a past event?

trip.prompt: Find the section on aspect particles and read one example for each.

stages.title: Complex sentence introduction
stages.hook: How do you say "although it is hard, I like it"? Linking pairs help you build longer sentences.
explain: Complex Chinese sentences often use paired words. 因为…所以… means because… so… and 虽然…但是… means although… but…. Unlike English, Chinese uses both halves together: 虽然我很累，但是我很开心 (although I am tired, I am happy).
如果…就… means if… then…: 如果下雨，我们就不去 (if it rains, we won't go). 不但…而且… means not only… but also…: 他不但聪明，而且努力 (he is not only clever but also hardworking).
Another useful pattern is 一边…一边… for two actions at once: 一边吃一边聊 (eat while chatting). In writing, use a comma between clauses and a full stop (。) at the end.
stages.mnemonic: Pairs travel together: 虽然…但是…, 如果…就….
sentences: Although I am tired, I am happy.
If it rains, we will not go.
He is not only clever but also hardworking.

gq.why: 虽然 pairs with 但是 or 可是.

gq.q: Which sentence means "If it rains, we will not go"?
o: 因为下雨，我们不去所以
gq.why: 如果 starts the condition and 就 starts the result.

panel.q: Why is it unusual in Mandarin to say only 虽然 without 但是?
panel.why: Mandarin normally uses both halves of the pair, while English uses only one of although/but.

panel.q: What does 不但…而且… add?
panel.why: It adds a second point as well as the first one.

panel.q: Which sentence uses 一边…一边… correctly?
panel.why: 一边…一边… joins two actions that happen at once.

teach.model: Mandarin often uses paired connectors, such as 因为…所以…, 虽然…但是… and 如果…就…. Where English uses only one word, Mandarin often uses both.

points.ask: What is the pair for because and so?
What is the pair for although?
What is the pair for if then?

trip.prompt: Find the section on conjunctions and list two pairs.

stages.title: Reading short stories
stages.hook: Many stories begin with "once upon a time". How do Chinese stories start, and how do they move on?
explain: Story words help you follow the order of events. 从前 (cóngqián) means once upon a time, 有一天 (yǒu yì tiān) means one day, 后来 (hòulái) means later, 突然 (tūrán) means suddenly, 于是 (yúshì) means so, and 最后 (zuìhòu) means finally.
When reading, look for the subject, the verb and the object first. Skip words you do not know and use the radicals and the pinyin to guess. Notice 了 for completed events and 的 for descriptions.
Chinese has many short folk tales and fables, and the moral is often stated in a short saying. Readers enjoy finding the moral at the end: 故事 (gùshi) means story and 结果 (jiéguǒ) means result.
stages.mnemonic: First 从前, then 有一天, then 突然, finally 最后.
sentences: Once upon a time there was a little rabbit.
One day he met a friend.
In the end everyone was happy.

gq.q: Which word starts a fairy tale?
gq.why: 从前 means once upon a time.

panel.q: A story says 于是他回家了. What does 于是 show?
o: A result of what came before
panel.why: 于是 shows that something follows from the previous event.

panel.q: What can you do first when a sentence has many unknown characters?
o: Find the main subject, verb and object
panel.why: Find the subject, verb and object, and use radicals to guess.

panel.q: Which order is the most natural for a story?
o: 最后, 从前, 后来
后来, 最后, 从前
突然, 最后, 从前
从前, 后来, 最后
panel.why: The usual story order is from the beginning to the end.

teach.model: Look for story words like 从前, 后来, 突然 and 最后 to follow the order. Find the subject, verb and object first. Use radicals and context to guess unknown words.

points.ask: What words show the order of events?
What should I find first?
How can I guess new characters?

trip.prompt: Find one Chinese fable and the moral it teaches.

stages.title: Listening comprehension
stages.hook: If you hear 我不是老师 very fast, how do you catch the key words?
explain: Listening in Mandarin means hearing tones as well as sounds. 听力 (tīnglì) is listening ability. Try to get the main idea (大意, dàyì) first, and then listen again for details. Ask for 重复 (chóngfù, repeat) if needed.

Several tone changes happen in real speech. When two third tones come together, the first is said as a second tone: 你好 is spoken nǐ hǎo but sounds like ní hǎo. 不 (bù) becomes bú before a fourth tone: 不是 is bú shì. 一 (yī) changes before other tones: 一个 is yí gè.
Fast speech also drops some sounds, and a speaker's regional accent can differ from the textbook. Listening to many different voices helps. Use a recording and replay it slowly.
stages.mnemonic: Listen big, then small: main idea, then details.

gq.q: How is 你好 usually pronounced in real speech?
gq.why: Two third tones in a row make the first rise: ní hǎo.

gq.q: What is the best first step when listening to a long recording?
gq.why: Get the main idea first and then listen for details.

panel.q: How is 不是 pronounced in speech?
panel.why: 不 changes to bú before a fourth tone.

panel.q: A learner hears a different accent and cannot understand. What helps?
panel.why: Hearing many speakers trains your ear to accents and variants.

panel.q: What is the purpose of 大意?
panel.why: 大意 means main idea, the overall point of what you heard.

teach.model: To listen well, find the main idea first and then listen for details. Tones can change in real speech, such as 你好 becoming ní hǎo. Hearing many speakers helps with accents.

points.ask: What should I listen for first?
What happens to tones in real speech?
How can I cope with accents?

trip.prompt: Find the third-tone sandhi rule and say 你好 aloud.

stages.title: Conversation and pronunciation
stages.hook: Which sounds in Mandarin are hardest for English speakers: zh, ch, sh, or q and x?
explain: Mandarin sounds are described by the initial (声母, shēngmǔ) and final (韵母, yùnmǔ). Compare b and p: b is unaspirated and p has a puff of air. In the same way d and t, g and k, z and c, zh and ch differ by that puff of air.

The "retroflex" sounds zh, ch, sh and r are made with the tongue curled slightly back, while z, c and s are made with the tongue flat behind the teeth. The sounds j, q and x are said with the tongue near the hard palate, and ü needs rounded lips like saying "ee".

Standard Mandarin (普通话, pǔtōnghuà) is the national standard, based on Beijing pronunciation. Some northern speakers add 儿化 (érhuà), an "r" ending, like 花儿 (huār). Local accents (口音, kǒuyīn) from other regions are normal and respected.
stages.mnemonic: Puff or no puff: b is quiet, p breathes out.
sentences: I practise speaking Mandarin every day.

gq.q: What makes p different from b in pinyin?
o: p has a puff of air
gq.why: p is aspirated, with a puff of air.

gq.q: Which pair of sounds is made with the tongue curled back?
gq.why: zh, ch, sh and r are retroflex.

panel.q: A learner says "sān" with zh. What is the problem?
o: They add a puff of air
They mix up retroflex and flat sounds
panel.why: zh and s are different sounds and would change the word.

panel.q: What is 普通话?
panel.why: It is the standard form of Mandarin taught in schools and used on the media.

panel.q: Why is érhuà heard more in northern China?
o: It is a feature of northern accents
panel.why: Beijing and northern speech use the r-ending more, while other regions use it less.

teach.model: Mandarin sounds are initials and finals. Some pairs differ only by a puff of air, such as b and p. The tongue is curled back for zh, ch, sh and r. The standard form is called 普通话.

points.ask: What differs between b and p?
How is zh made?
What is the standard form called?

trip.prompt: Find a chart of the initials in pinyin and read the aspirated and unaspirated pairs.

stages.title: Writing paragraphs
stages.hook: How do you start a paragraph and link your ideas in Chinese? Some small words do a lot.
explain: A good paragraph in Chinese has a main idea, a few support sentences and a closing. Connecting words help the reader. 首先 (shǒuxiān) means first, 然后 (ránhòu) means then, 另外 (lìngwài) means in addition, 例如 (lìrú) means for example and 总之 (zǒngzhī) means in short.

Chinese punctuation is written as full-width marks: the full stop is 。, the comma is ，, the pause comma used in lists is 、, the question mark is ？ and the exclamation mark is ！. Quotation marks are “ ” in simplified Chinese. Traditionally, a new paragraph starts with two blank character spaces.
When writing, keep short sentences first and do not mix 的, 得 and 地 randomly: 的 links a noun, 地 links a verb, and 得 comes after a verb. For example 高兴地说 (say happily) and 说得很好 (speak well).
stages.mnemonic: First, then, also, for example, in short: 首先, 然后, 另外, 例如, 总之.
sentences: First I get up, then I eat breakfast.
In short, I like my school.

gq.q: Which mark is the Chinese full stop?
gq.why: The Chinese full stop is a small circle, 。.

gq.q: Which word begins a closing sentence?
gq.why: 总之 means in short and is often used to summarise.

panel.q: What is the use of 、?
o: To separate items in a list
panel.why: It is the enumeration comma used between items in a list.

panel.q: Which sentence uses 得 correctly?
panel.why: 得 comes after a verb to describe how it is done.

panel.q: A student begins every sentence with 然后. What is the better writing choice?
panel.why: Using a variety of linkers makes a paragraph clearer.

teach.model: A paragraph begins with a main idea, adds support with words like 首先 and 例如, and ends with 总之. Use Chinese punctuation: 。 for a full stop and ， for a comma.

points.ask: Which words link my ideas?
What is the full stop?
How do I end?

trip.prompt: Find the table of Chinese punctuation marks and compare with English.

stages.title: Cultural expressions and idioms
stages.hook: What do people in China say before an exam, at a New Year meal or when thanking someone for effort?
explain: Many Chinese expressions are about courtesy and encouragement. 加油 (jiāyóu) literally means add oil, and is used to cheer someone on. 辛苦了 (xīnkǔ le) means you worked hard, said to thank someone for effort. 恭喜 (gōngxǐ) means congratulations.

At the Spring Festival, people say 新年快乐 or 恭喜发财. When treating guests, people often say 请客 (qǐngkè), to invite someone and pay. Politeness (客气, kèqi) sometimes means refusing a gift once or twice before accepting.

The idea of 面子 (miànzi, face) is also important: it is about dignity and respect. A polite way to ask for help is 麻烦你了 (máfan nǐ le), meaning sorry to trouble you. These expressions cannot always be translated word by word.
stages.mnemonic: 加油: add oil to the engine of a friend!
sentences: I wish you a happy new year.
Good luck, you can do it.

gq.q: A friend runs a race. What do you shout?
Someone finishes a long job. Which is a natural thank-you?
gq.why: 辛苦了 thanks someone for hard work.

panel.q: Why does 加油 not mean literally add oil here?
panel.why: It is an idiom that has become a general cheer, not meant literally.

panel.q: A host insists on paying for dinner and the guest first refuses politely. Why?
o: They do not like the food
panel.why: Refusing once or twice is a courteous custom (客气).

panel.q: What is the best reply to 恭喜你！?
panel.why: The reply is a thank-you: 谢谢.

teach.model: Many expressions carry politeness, such as 加油 to cheer, 辛苦了 to thank for effort and 恭喜 to congratulate. The meaning is not always word-for-word, so learn the situation too.

points.ask: What do I say to cheer?
What do I say to thank for effort?
Can I translate them word by word?

trip.prompt: Find a custom around greetings or gifts in China.

stages.title: Practical travel communication
stages.hook: You arrive in a new city. How do you ask where the toilet is, or how to get to the station?
explain: Travel words: 机场 (jīchǎng) airport, 火车站 (huǒchēzhàn) train station, 地铁 (dìtiě) metro, 出租车 (chūzūchē) taxi, 酒店 (jiǔdiàn) hotel, 护照 (hùzhào) passport, 车票 (chēpiào) ticket and 洗手间 (xǐshǒujiān) toilet.

To ask for a place, say 请问，…在哪儿？ (excuse me, where is…?). To say you want to go, use 我要去… To ask about transport, say 怎么走？ (how do I get there?). Directions use 左 (left), 右 (right) and 直走 (go straight).
In large cities, you may need to show your passport at stations and hotels. Train tickets are often bought with an app or at a machine, so keep your 护照 with you, and ask politely: 请问，这趟车去北京吗？
stages.mnemonic: 请问 + place + 在哪儿 gets you almost anywhere.
sentences: Excuse me, where is the toilet?
I want to go to the train station.
I would like to book a room.

gq.q: Which phrase asks "Where is the station?"
gq.why: 在哪儿 asks where something is.
直 means straight, 走 means walk or go.

panel.q: You want to be polite when asking a stranger. What do you begin with?
panel.why: 请问 is a polite way to start a question to a stranger.

panel.q: Which word would you need at a hotel check-in?
panel.why: You usually show your passport (护照).

panel.q: Which is the better sentence to say you want to go to the airport?
panel.why: 我要去 plus the place says you want to go there.

teach.model: To ask for a place say 请问 and then the place with 在哪儿. To say where you want to go use 我要去. Keep your passport for hotels and stations.

points.ask: How do I start politely?
How do I ask where something is?
How do I say where I want to go?

trip.prompt: Find how long-distance trains are described and name one famous line.
